definitions.explanation: A gift given at the end of the year (typically December) to express gratitude to people who have helped you throughout the year.

examples.japanese: {取引先|とりひきさき}にお{歳暮|せいぼ}を{送|おく}る。
examples.english: To send a year-end gift to a business client.

examples.japanese: お{歳暮|せいぼ}の{時期|じき}になると{宅配便|たくはいびん}が{忙|いそが}しくなる。
examples.english: Delivery services get busy during the year-end gift season.

examples.japanese: {毎年|まいとし}お{歳暮|せいぼ}にハムを{贈|おく}っている。
examples.english: Every year I send ham as a year-end gift.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
{歳暮|せいぼ} literally means "year's end." The お is an honorific prefix.

TIMING:
- Early to mid-December
- Should arrive before the New Year
- Often sent earlier than お{中元|ちゅうげん} in the gift-giving cycle

COMMON GIFTS:
- Ham and meat products
- Seafood (crab, salmon roe)
- Sweets and confections
- Sake, beer, or other beverages

COMPARISON WITH お{中元|ちゅうげん}:
- お{歳暮|せいぼ} is often considered slightly more important
- If giving only one, お{歳暮|せいぼ} is typically prioritized
- Same recipients and similar value range (3,000-5,000 yen)

MODERN TRENDS:
The custom is declining somewhat among younger generations, but remains important in business relationships.
